there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession
The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession

interpretation_limits: In a license setting, the supplied opinion also states that the tenant is not said to part with possession unless the arrangement wholly ousts the tenant from legal possession of that part.
The supplied law does not state whether that license formulation is exhaustive for every possible arrangement.

tests.text: For the parting-with-possession route, the tenant retains legal possession of the relevant part where there is concurrent user or mere use by others without wholly ousting the tenant from legal possession of that part.

source_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself
A tenant cannot be said to part with the possession of any part of the premises unless his agreement with the license wholly ousts him from the legal possession of that part.

interpretation_limits: This is a defeating qualification only for the parting-with-possession route; the supplied material does not say it independently resolves subletting or assignment.
The supplied material does not define every factual circumstance in which legal possession is retained.

rules.text: Notwithstanding contrary law or contract, the supplied statute states a baseline against recovery of possession, with the Controller able to order recovery on a prescribed application and specified grounds only.

source_refs.quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law or contract, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made by any court or Controller in favour of the landlord against a tenant
the Controller may, on an application made to him in the prescribed manner, make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on one or more of the following grounds only

rules.text: A supplied s14(1)(b) ground is post-9-June-1952 subletting, assignment, or other parting with possession of the whole or any part of the premises without the landlord's written consent.

source_refs.quote: that the tenant has, on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;

rules.text: Subletting, assignment, and otherwise parting with possession are distinct concepts applying to different circumstances.

source_refs.quote: These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

rules.text: Subletting requires the landlord-and-tenant relationship and tenancy incidents identified in the supplied opinion.

source_refs.quote: In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.

rules.text: Assignment requires the tenant to divest himself of all rights held as tenant.

source_refs.quote: In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

rules.text: Parting with possession requires tenant-caused vesting of possession in another with divestment or abandonment of the tenant's right to possession; mere or concurrent use while the tenant retains legal possession does not itself amount to parting.
